properties.areaDesc: Coastal Duval; Coastal Flagler; Southeast Coastal St. Johns
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 23 at 12:46AM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler and Southeast Coastal
St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, from late tonight through Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Johnson County/Casper BLM
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 22 at 10:45PM MDT until October 23 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low Humidities...Unseasonably Warm Temperatures...
Strong Gusty Winds...and Wind Shift with a Cold Front could
cause erratic fire behavior.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In North Central WY...Fire Weather Zone 281.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In North Central WY...Johnson.

* COLD FRONT: Moves in after 6 PM MDT Friday, with northwesterly 20
to 30 mph winds and gusts up to 40 mph.

* WIND: Southwest 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 20 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Highs in the upper 60s.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TO 8 PM MDT FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula
properties.headline: Blizzard Warning issued October 22 at 8:41PM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions expected. Total snow accumulations
between 1 and 3 inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Baldwin Peninsula and Lower Kobuk Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility. Visibilities may drop below
a quarter mile due to falling and blowing snow. Very strong winds
could result in power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow and gusty winds will produce blizzard
conditions Friday. As south winds continue and temperatures warm,
snow will transition to rain potentially as early as Friday
evening. Strongest wind gusts will be Friday afternoon into early
Saturday morning.
properties.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.

NWSheadline: BLIZZARD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM FRIDAY TO 4 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 23 at 12:36AM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. The advisory will either need to be extended into
next week or upgraded to a warning Sunday into Monday when
King Tides peak and rain chances and onshore winds are
highest. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
